units.zh: 郤詵
units.en: Xi Shen.
units.literal: Xi Shen.

units.zh: 郤詵，字廣基，濟陰單父人也。
units.en: Xi Shen, courtesy name Guangji, came from Shanfu in Jiyin commandery.
units.literal: Xi Shen, style Guangji, was a man of Shanfu in Jiyin.

units.zh: 父晞，尚書左丞。
units.en: His father, Xi, served as Assistant Director of the Left of the Secretariat.
units.literal: His father Xi was Assistant Director of the Left of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 詵博學多才，瑰偉倜儻，不拘細行，州郡禮命並不應。
units.en: Shen was learned and gifted, striking in bearing and heedless of minor proprieties; he turned down every formal appointment offered by local authorities.
units.literal: Shen was broadly learned and multi-talented, magnificent in stature and free and unconventional, not bound by petty conduct; he did not respond to ceremonial summons from prefecture or commandery.

units.zh: 泰始中，詔天下舉賢良直言之士，太守文立舉詵應選。
units.en: During the Taishi reign, an edict called on the empire to recommend worthy men who would speak candidly; Prefect Wen Li nominated Shen to take part.
units.literal: In the Taishi era, an edict ordered the realm to recommend worthy men prepared to speak plainly; Prefect Wen Li recommended Shen to answer the summons.

units.zh: 詔曰：「蓋太上以德撫時，易簡無文。
units.en: The edict ran: "In remotest antiquity the sage ruler steadied the age through virtue; governance stayed plain and unadorned.
units.literal: An edict said: "In highest antiquity the supreme ruler soothed the age through virtue; rule was easy and plain, without elaborate culture.

units.zh: 至於三代，禮樂大備，制度彌繁。
units.en: By the Three Dynasties, ritual and music had been brought to full elaboration and regulation grew ever denser.
units.literal: By the Three Dynasties, ritual and music were fully prepared, and institutions became ever more intricate.

units.zh: 文質之變，其理何由？
units.en: What principle governs the swing between outward refinement and inward simplicity?
units.literal: As refinement and simplicity alternate, what is the underlying principle?

units.zh: 虞、夏之際，聖明系踵，而損益不同。
units.en: From Yu to Xia, sagely rulers succeeded one another in close succession, yet each borrowed from his predecessor in a different measure.
units.literal: Between the eras of Yu and Xia, sagely and enlightened rulers followed one upon another, yet their reductions and augmentations differed.

units.zh: 周道既衰，仲尼猶曰從周。
units.en: Even after the Zhou order decayed, Confucius insisted he would follow the Zhou model.
units.literal: When the way of Zhou had declined, Confucius still said he would follow Zhou.

units.zh: 因革之宜，又何殊也？
units.en: When to preserve and when to reform—why should the right measure ever be wholly different?
units.literal: When circumstances call for continuity or for reform, wherein lies any fundamental difference in what is fitting?

units.zh: 聖王既沒，遺制猶存，霸者迭興而翼輔之，王道之缺，其無補乎？
units.en: After the sage kings were gone, their institutions lingered; hegemons rose one after another and propped them up—did that never repair what the royal way lacked?
units.literal: After the sage kings passed away, their inherited regulations remained; hegemons arose in succession and lent them support—did this never remedy the deficiencies of the true kingly way?

units.zh: 何陵遲之不反也？
units.en: Why, then, did decline never turn back?
units.literal: Why did decline never reverse?

units.zh: 豈霸德之淺歟？
units.en: Was hegemonic virtue simply too shallow?
units.literal: Was it because hegemonic virtue was shallow?

units.zh: 期運不可致歟？
units.en: Or because the times could not be forced?
units.literal: Or because the appointed times could not be forced?

units.zh: 且夷吾之智，而功止于霸，何哉？
units.en: Guan Zhong was formidably capable—why did his accomplishment never rise beyond hegemony?
units.literal: Moreover, Guan Zhong was so wise—why did his achievement stop at hegemony?

units.zh: 夫昔人之為政，革亂亡之弊，建不刊之統，移風易俗，刑措不用，豈非化之盛歟？
units.en: The ancients took power amid ruin, forged an enduring order, reshaped customs until punishments were laid aside—was that not transformation at its fullest?
units.literal: When men of old governed, they reformed the maladies of chaos and ruin, founded an imperishable norm, shifted customs and changed habits, and punishments fell into disuse—was this not the height of transformation?

units.zh: 何修而向茲？
units.en: What must a ruler cultivate to reach that?
units.literal: What must be cultivated to attain such a state?

units.zh: 朕獲承祖宗之休烈，於茲七載，而人未服訓，政道罔述。
units.en: I have received my forebears' glorious legacy; seven years have passed, yet the people still resist moral instruction and I have failed to set forth how government ought to run.
units.literal: We have inherited the splendid legacy of Our ancestors; seven years have passed, yet the people are not yet disciplined by instruction, and the way of government has not been articulated.

units.zh: 以古況今，何不相逮之遠也？
units.en: Measured against antiquity, why do we fall so terribly short?
units.literal: Comparing antiquity with the present, why is the distance between them so far from being reached?

units.zh: 雖明之弗及，猶思與群賢慮之，將何以辨所聞之疑昧，獲至論於讜言乎？
units.en: Though I am less discerning than the ancients, I still wish to think this through with you—how am I to clear what puzzles me and hear sound doctrine from honest counsel?
units.literal: Though Our clarity does not match theirs, We still wish to deliberate with the throng of worthies—how may We resolve the doubts We have heard and obtain the highest doctrine from candid speech?

units.zh: 加自頃戎狄內侵，災害屢作，邊氓流離，征夫苦役，豈政刑之謬，將有司非其任歟？
units.en: Moreover, barbarians have lately crossed the frontier, disasters keep coming, border people are scattered, and soldiers buckle under the levy—is that bad policy and harsh law, or men unfit for office?
units.literal: Moreover, since barbarians have lately invaded within the borders and disasters have struck repeatedly, frontier folk have been uprooted and conscripts worn down by corvée—is this owing to errors in policy and punishments, or to officers not suited to their posts?

units.zh: 各悉乃心，究而論之。
units.en: Each of you search your conscience and lay out your reasoning fully.
units.literal: Each of you exhaust your minds and discuss it thoroughly.

units.zh: 上明古制，下切當今。
units.en: Explain the classical models above and speak squarely to conditions today below.
units.literal: Above, clarify ancient institutions; below, cut to present realities.

units.zh: 朕之失德，所宜振補。
units.en: Where I have fallen short in virtue is precisely what must be set right.
units.literal: Where We have failed in virtue is what ought to be remedied and repaired.

units.zh: 其正議無隱，將敬聽之。」
units.en: Speak plainly and withhold nothing of your honest judgment—I shall receive it with respect."
units.literal: Speak your upright counsel without concealment; We shall listen to it with respect."

units.zh: 詵對曰：
units.en: Xi Shen replied:
units.literal: Shen replied:

units.zh: 伏惟陛下以聖德君臨，猶垂意於博采，故招賢正之士，而臣等薄陋，不足以降大問也。
units.en: I reflect that Your Majesty, enthroned in sage virtue, still troubles to cast the net wide for counsel and summons worthy men to speak plainly—yet we who stand before you are men of slight talent, unequal to so weighty a theme.
units.literal: I humbly reflect that Your Majesty, though ruling as sovereign in sage virtue, still deigns to cast your mind wide and gather counsel; hence you summon worthy men of upright speech—yet we your servants are shallow and mean, not sufficient to lower so great a question to us.

units.zh: 是以竊有自疑之心，雖致身于闕庭，亦ＦＣ俯矣。
units.en: So I doubt my own fitness; though I have come to the palace gate, I remain ill at ease and abashed before you.
units.literal: Hence I privately harbor doubt about myself; though I have presented myself at the palace gate, I am still abashed and bowed low.

units.zh: 伏讀聖策，乃知下問之旨篤焉。
units.en: Once I had reverently read Your examination theme, I understood how deeply earnest Your question was.
units.literal: Having reverently read the sacred examination theme, I then knew how earnest was the intent of Your inquiry below.

units.zh: 臣聞上古推賢讓位，教同德一，故易簡而人化；
units.en: I have heard that in earliest times worthies abdicated in favor of merit and teaching aimed at a single shared virtue—so governance stayed plain and the people were shaped without fuss.
units.literal: I have heard that in high antiquity worthies yielded their thrones and instruction was of one virtue; hence rule was easy and plain and the people were transformed.

units.zh: 三代世及，季末相承，故文繁而後整。
units.en: Under the Three Dynasties the throne passed by inheritance, each late age handing on to the next—so outward forms multiplied and only afterward could they be disciplined.
units.literal: Through the Three Dynasties succession passed within families, and late ages inherited one from another; hence culture grew elaborate and afterward had to be set in order.

units.zh: 虞、夏之相因，而損益不同，非帝王之道異，救弊之路殊也。
units.en: Yu and Xia built on what came before, yet each adjusted the pattern differently—not because the royal way itself changed, but because each age took its own path out of decay.
units.literal: The succession from Yu to Xia borrowed from one another, yet reduction and augmentation differed—not because the way of the sage kings differed, but because the roads to remedy evil were distinct.

units.zh: 周當二代之流，承凋偽之極，盡禮樂之致，窮制度之理，其文詳備，仲尼因時宜而曰從周，非殊論也。
units.en: Zhou followed two earlier houses at a time of extreme decay and fraud; it carried ritual and music to their fullest expression and worked out institutions to their logical limit—its forms were complete in every detail. Confucius, judging what the age needed, said he would follow Zhou; that was no inconsistent doctrine.
units.literal: Zhou stood in the current after two dynasties, inheriting extreme withering and deceit; it exhausted the utmost of ritual and music and fathomed the rationale of institutions—its pattern was detailed and complete. Confucius, responding to what the times required, said he would follow Zhou; this was not a contradictory judgment.

units.zh: 臣聞聖王之化先禮樂，五霸之興勤政刑。
units.en: Sage kings began transformation with ritual and music; the Five Hegemons rose by driving government and punishments hard.
units.literal: I have heard that sage kings transformed others first through ritual and music, whereas the rise of the Five Hegemons lay in diligent government and punishments.

units.zh: 禮樂之化深，政刑之用淺。
units.en: Ritual and music work deep in the character; law and punishment operate on the surface.
units.literal: The transforming power of ritual and music runs deep; the application of government and punishments is shallow.

units.zh: 勤之則可以小安，墮之則遂陵遲。
units.en: Push the latter course hard and you may win a little calm; let it slip and decline sets in without fail.
units.literal: If you labor at the latter, you may gain a little peace; if you let it slip, decline follows inexorably.

units.zh: 所由之路本近，故所補之功不侔也。
units.en: The two approaches start from nearly the same ground, yet the good they can accomplish is not comparable.
units.literal: The paths they spring from lie fundamentally close together; hence the good they can mend is not equal.

units.zh: 而齊桓失之葵丘，夷吾淪於小器，功止於霸，不亦宜乎！
units.en: Duke Huan failed at the Kuiqiu covenant; Guan Zhong proved a limited instrument—his achievement stopped at hegemony. Small wonder!
units.literal: Thus Duke Huan of Qi missed the mark at Kuiqiu, and Guan Zhong sank to the measure of a petty vessel—his merit stopping at hegemony: was it not fitting!

units.zh: 策曰：「建不刊之統，移風易俗，使天下洽和，何修而向茲？」
units.en: Your examination asked: "To found an enduring order, to shift customs and change habits until the realm is at peace—what must be cultivated to attain that?"
units.literal: The policy question said: "To establish an imperishable norm, to shift customs and change habits, and to make all under Heaven harmonious—what must be cultivated to reach this?"

units.zh: 臣以為莫大於擇人而官之也。
units.en: I answer that nothing matters more than choosing the right men and putting them in office.
units.literal: I submit that nothing is greater than selecting men and assigning them to office.

units.zh: 今之典刑，匪無一統，宰牧之才，優劣異績，或以之興，或以之替，此蓋人能弘政非政弘人也。
units.en: Our laws are not without a single framework, yet among those who rule counties and commanderies, talent varies and results differ—some flourish under the system, some founder—because men give force to policy, not policy to men.
units.literal: Today's statutes and models are not without a unified framework, yet among the talents of governors and shepherds, merit varies and performance differs—some rise through them, some fail through them—this is because men can enlarge government, not because government enlarges men.

units.zh: 舍人務政，雖勤何益？
units.en: Neglect the men and chase empty policy—what good will mere diligence do?
units.literal: If you neglect men and pursue policy alone, what benefit comes from diligence?

units.zh: 臣竊觀乎古今，而考其美惡：古人相與求賢，今人相與求爵。
units.en: Comparing past and present, I find this contrast: antiquity joined hands to find worthy men; today men join hands to chase titles.
units.literal: I have privately surveyed past and present and weighed what was admirable and what was base: the ancients cooperated to seek worthies; men today cooperate to seek noble rank.

units.zh: 古之官人，君責之於上，臣舉之於下，得其人有賞，失其人有罰，安得不求賢乎！
units.en: When the ancients filled offices, the ruler held officials accountable from above while ministers nominated from below—reward for a good pick, punishment for a bad one—how could they fail to seek real talent?
units.literal: In antiquity, when appointing officers, the ruler demanded results above and ministers recommended below; obtaining the right man brought reward, missing him brought punishment—how could they not seek worthies?

units.zh: 今之官者，父兄營之，親戚助之，有人事則通，無人事則塞，安得不求爵乎！
units.en: Today office-seekers have fathers and brothers pull strings and kin lend leverage—pull opens doors, isolation leaves you shut out—how could men not scramble after titles?
units.literal: Today, when seeking office, fathers and elder brothers scheme for it, kin lend aid—where personal connections exist, things open; where they do not, they are blocked—how can men not chase noble rank?

units.zh: 賢苟求達，達在修道，窮在失義，故靜以待之也。
units.en: The worthy man who seeks recognition finds it by cultivating the Way; he falls obscure only by betraying right principle—so he waits in quiet self-command.
units.literal: For the worthy, if advancement is what is sought, advancement lies in cultivating the way, and obscurity lies in abandoning right principle—hence they keep still and await their time.

units.zh: 爵苟可求，得在進取，失在後時，故動以要之也。
units.en: Rank, when it can be chased, goes to whoever pushes first and slips from whoever arrives late—so men scramble and grasp.
units.literal: For noble rank, if it can be chased, obtaining lies in pressing forward, and losing lies in lagging behind—hence they stir and grasp for it.

units.zh: 動則爭競，爭競則朋黨，朋黨則誣誷，誣誷則臧否失實，真偽相冒，主聽用惑，奸之所會也。
units.en: Scrambling breeds rivalry, rivalry breeds factions, factions breed slander—praise and blame lose touch with reality, truth and falsehood blur together, the ruler's judgment clouds in appointments, and treachery finds its opening.
units.literal: Stirring breeds rivalry; rivalry breeds factions; factions breed slander; slander makes praise and blame miss the truth and false and true mingle—the ruler's hearing is confused in employment—this is where treachery gathers.

units.zh: 靜則貞固，貞固則正直，正直則信讓，信讓則推賢，推賢不伐，相下無厭，主聽用察，德之所趣也。
units.en: Quiet brings steadfastness, steadfastness brings integrity, integrity brings trust and deference, trust yields room for worthier men—recommend without boasting, defer without resentment, and the ruler hears clearly when he appoints; there virtue gathers.
units.literal: Stillness yields steadfastness; steadfastness yields uprightness; uprightness yields good faith and deference; good faith and deference yield recommending the worthy; recommending without boasting and yielding without weariness clarify the ruler's hearing in employment—this is where virtue gathers.

units.zh: 故能使之靜，雖日高枕而人自正；
units.en: Hold men to that stillness and you may prop your pillow all day—the people will set themselves right.
units.literal: Therefore if you can keep men still, though daily you lean high on your pillow, people will correct themselves.

units.zh: 不能禁動，雖復夙夜，俗不一也。
units.en: Fail to stop the scrambling and you may toil from dawn to dusk—customs will never unify.
units.literal: If you cannot restrain stirring, though again you toil morning and night, customs will not become one.

units.zh: 且人無愚智，咸慕名宦，莫不飾正于外，藏邪於內，故邪正之人難得而知也。
units.en: Wise or foolish, all chase reputation and office—everyone polishes virtue on the surface while hiding deviance within—so you cannot easily tell straight men from crooked.
units.literal: Moreover, men without distinction of foolish or wise alike covet fame and office; none fail to adorn rectitude outwardly while hiding deviance within—hence the crooked and the upright are hard to know.

units.zh: 任得其正，則眾正益至；
units.en: Employ one upright man and more upright men will come.
units.literal: If you employ the upright, then the many upright will increasingly arrive.

units.zh: 若得其邪，則眾邪亦集。
units.en: Pick a crooked man and crooked men flock to him.
units.literal: If you obtain the crooked, then the many crooked also gather.

units.zh: 物繁其類，誰能止之！
units.en: Like calls to like—who can halt it?
units.literal: Things swarm with their kind—who can stop it!

units.zh: 故亡國失世者，未嘗不為眾邪所積也。
units.en: States that fell and ages that ended always piled error upon error until wrong consumed them.
units.literal: Hence those who lost their state and missed their age never failed to pile up a multitude of the crooked.

units.zh: 方其初作，必始於微，微而不絕，其終乃著。
units.en: Evil begins small; leave the small unchecked and the end is plain for all to see.
units.literal: When wrongdoing first arises, it always begins from what is minute; if what is minute is not cut off, in the end it becomes manifest.

units.zh: 天地不能頓為寒暑，人主亦不能頓為隆替。
units.en: Heaven and earth do not flip from winter to summer in an instant; neither does a ruler vault from glory to ruin overnight.
units.literal: Heaven and earth cannot suddenly become cold or heat; neither can the ruler suddenly become glorious or declined.

units.zh: 故寒暑漸於春秋，隆替起於得失。
units.en: Cold and warmth creep in through spring and autumn; rise and fall grow out of getting policy right or wrong.
units.literal: Hence cold and heat advance gradually through spring and autumn; glory and decline arise from getting or losing the right course.

units.zh: 當今之世，宦者無關梁，邪門啟矣；
units.en: Today aspirants to office meet no checkpoint—the crooked road lies wide open.
units.literal: In the present age, office-seekers face no barrier passes—the gate to deviance stands open.

units.zh: 朝廷不責賢，正路塞矣。
units.en: The court never holds anyone accountable for recommending talent—the straight path is shut.
units.literal: The court does not hold worthies accountable—the straight road is blocked.

units.zh: 得失之源，何以甚此！
units.en: At the root of success and failure, what could exceed this!
units.literal: The source of gain and loss—how could it be worse than this!

units.zh: 所謂責賢，使之相舉也；
units.en: What I mean by accountability for worthies is mutual recommendation.
units.literal: What is called holding worthies accountable is making them recommend one another.

units.zh: 所謂關梁，使之相保也。
units.en: What I mean by barrier posts is mutual surety.
units.literal: What is called barrier passes is making them guarantee one another.

units.zh: 賢不舉則有咎，保不信則有罰。
units.en: Fail to raise a worthy man and you answer for it; give a false guarantee and you pay the penalty.
units.literal: If worthies are not recommended, there is blame; if guarantors are untrustworthy, there is punishment.

units.zh: 故古者諸侯必貢士，不貢者削，貢而不適亦削。
units.en: So in old times every feudal lord owed the throne a quota of scholars—miss the quota and your fief was cut; send an unsuitable man and it was cut again.
units.literal: Hence in antiquity each feudal lord had to present tribute of scholars; those who did not present had their domains reduced, and those who presented but were unsuitable also had their domains reduced.

units.zh: 夫士者，難知也；
units.en: Talent is hard to judge.
units.literal: As for scholars, they are hard to know.

units.zh: 不適者，薄過也。
units.en: Missing the mark is a light offense.
units.literal: "Unsuitable" means a slight fault.

units.zh: 不得不責，強其所不知也；
units.en: Yet you must demand results—so you force men to vouch for those they cannot truly know.
units.literal: You must demand results—this forces what they do not know.

units.zh: 罰其所不適，深其薄過，非恕也。
units.en: Punish that miss harshly and you punish a venial fault severely—that is not magnanimous rule.
units.literal: Punishing them for unsuitability—deepening blame for a slight fault—is not forgiving policy.

units.zh: 且天子于諸侯，有不純臣之義，斯責之矣。
units.en: Moreover, Son of Heaven and feudal lords do not stand in the plain relation of sovereign to subject—yet even so such demands were laid on them.
units.literal: Moreover, as between Son of Heaven and feudal lords there is the principle that they are not "pure ministers"; on this account such accountability is imposed.

units.zh: 施行之道，寧縱不濫之矣。
units.en: In practice the rule was leniency before severity—better too loose than too harsh.
units.literal: In the way of applying such measures, one would rather err on the side of indulgence than of severity.

units.zh: 今皆反是，何也？
units.en: Today everything runs the opposite way—why?
units.literal: Today all this is reversed—why?

units.zh: 夫賢者天地之紀，品物之宗，其急之也，故寧濫以得之，無縱以失之也。
units.en: Worthy men are Heaven and Earth's measure and the root of every calling; need them desperately—better cast the net wide and catch them than indulge slackness and lose them.
units.literal: Worthy men are the bond of Heaven and earth and the ancestor of all things in their kinds; because they are urgently needed, better be inclusive and gain them than indulgent and lose them.

units.zh: 今則不然，世之悠悠者，各自取辨耳。
units.en: Today it is otherwise—everyone who drifts with the fashion grabs whatever argument suits him.
units.literal: Now it is not so—those who drift at ease with the age each take their own distinction.

units.zh: 故其材行並不可必，於公則政事紛亂。
units.en: So neither talent nor conduct can be trusted—in public life policy dissolves into chaos.
units.literal: Hence their talent and conduct alike cannot be relied upon; in public affairs government falls into confusion.

units.zh: 於私則污穢狼籍。
units.en: In private life they leave filth and scandal strewn behind them.
units.literal: In private life filth spreads in disorder.

units.zh: 自頃長吏特多此累，有亡命而被購懸者矣，有縛束而絞戮者矣。
units.en: Lately district magistrates especially pile up such stains—some are wanted men with price on their heads, some end bound on the scaffold.
units.literal: Of late district magistrates especially abound in such faults—some are wanted fugitives with reward posted, some have been bound and strangled or executed.

units.zh: 貪鄙竊位，不知誰升之者？
units.en: Venal men steal office—who handed them their seals?
units.literal: The greedy and base steal office—who promoted them?

units.zh: 獸兕出檻，不知誰可咎者？
units.en: When beasts break from their cages—whom do we hold accountable?
units.literal: When rhinoceroses and buffaloes escape their pens—whom may one blame?

units.zh: 漏網吞舟，何以過此！
units.en: The net gapes wide enough to swallow a boat—what crime could be worse!
units.literal: A leaking net swallows even a boat—what fault could exceed this!

units.zh: 人之於利，如蹈水火焉。
units.en: Men rush toward profit as if into fire or deep water.
units.literal: Men's relation to profit is like stepping into fire or water.

units.zh: 前人雖敗，後人復起，如彼此無已，誰止之者？
units.en: One crop of climbers falls and another rises—if that cycle never stops, who can arrest it?
units.literal: Though those before fail, those after rise again; if this alternation never ends, who stops it?

units.zh: 風流日競，誰憂之者？
units.en: The scramble worsens by the day—who even mourns it?
units.literal: As competitive striving grows daily, who grieves over it?

units.zh: 雖今聖思勞於夙夜，所使為政，恆得此屬，欲聖世化美俗平，亦俟河之清耳。
units.en: Though Your Majesty racks mind and body night and day, the men you send to govern are always of this stamp—to hope for a sage reign of polished customs is to wait till the Yellow River runs clear.
units.literal: Though now sacred thought labors morning and night, those charged with government constantly obtain this sort; desiring a sage age of transformed beauty and level customs is also waiting for the Yellow River to run clear.

units.zh: 若欲善之，宜創舉賢之典，峻關梁之防。
units.en: If you mean to mend this, establish clear rules for recommending worthies and tighten the gates at the passes.
units.literal: If you wish to improve this, you ought to institute statutes that enshrine recommending worthies and heighten the defenses of barrier passes.

units.zh: 其制既立，則人慎其舉而不苟，則賢者可知。
units.en: Once those rules are fixed, men will recommend with care and avoid careless picks—then worthies show themselves.
units.literal: Once the regulations stand, men will be cautious in whom they recommend and will not act recklessly—then the worthy can be known.

units.zh: 知賢而試，則官得其人矣。
units.en: Identify worthies and try them in office—then each post receives the right man.
units.literal: Know the worthy and test them—then offices will obtain the right men.

units.zh: 官得其人，則事得其序；
units.en: Right men in office bring affairs into proper order.
units.literal: When offices obtain the right men, affairs obtain their proper sequence.

units.zh: 事得其序，則物得其宜；
units.en: Orderly government lets each thing find its proper place.
units.literal: When affairs obtain their sequence, things obtain what is appropriate to them.

units.zh: 物得其宜，則生生豐植，人用資給，和樂興焉。
units.en: When everything sits right, life flourishes, people have enough to live on, and harmony spreads.
units.literal: When things obtain what is appropriate to them, then life multiplies and thrives, people find material sufficiency, and harmony and joy arise.

units.zh: 是故寡過而遠刑，知恥以近禮，此所以建不刊之統，移風易俗，刑措而不用也。
units.en: Faults dwindle and punishments fade; shame draws men toward ritual—this is how an enduring order is built, customs reshaped, and the rack left to gather dust.
units.literal: Hence faults are few and punishments lie far off; knowing shame draws near to ritual—this is how one establishes an imperishable norm, shifts customs and changes habits, and leaves punishments laid aside unused.

units.zh: 策曰：「自頃夷狄內侵，災眚屢降，將所任非其人乎？
units.en: Your examination asked: "Barbarians have lately crossed inward and disasters keep striking—is that because we put the wrong men in charge?
units.literal: The policy question said: "Since barbarians have lately invaded within our borders and calamities have repeatedly descended—is it because those entrusted are not the right men?

units.zh: 何由而至此？」
units.en: What chain of causes brought us here?"
units.literal: By what cause has it come to this?"

units.zh: 臣聞蠻夷猾夏，則皋陶作士，此欲善其末，則先其本也。
units.en: I have heard that when outer tribes troubled the heartland, Gaoyao was made Minister of Crime—to mend the branches you must heal the root first.
units.literal: I have heard that when the Man and Yi barbarians molested the Xia lands, then Gaoyao served as Minister of Crime—this means if you wish to improve the branches, you must first attend to the root.

units.zh: 夫任賢則政惠，使能則刑恕。
units.en: Employ worthies and policy grows humane; use the capable and punishments stay mild.
units.literal: Employ the worthy and government is kind; use the capable and punishments are lenient.

units.zh: 政惠則下仰其施，刑恕則人懷其勇。
units.en: Humane government wins gratitude below; lenient law lets men trust in its firmness.
units.literal: When government is kind, those below look up to its bounty; when punishments are lenient, men cherish its courage.

units.zh: 施以殖其財，勇以結其心。
units.en: Bounty fills their granaries; steadfast justice binds their loyalty.
units.literal: With bounty they multiply their wealth; with courage they bind their hearts.

units.zh: 故人居則資贍而知方，動則親上而志勇。
units.en: So at home they have enough to live on and know their duty; when mobilized they cling to their rulers and fight with courage.
units.literal: Hence when people dwell at rest they have material sufficiency and know their duty; when they move to action they cleave to superiors and their resolve is brave.

units.zh: 苟思其利而除其害，以生道利之者，雖死不貳；
units.en: Lead them by what preserves life—ease their harms and advance their good—and they will not waver even unto death;
units.literal: If they ponder its benefit and remove its harm, benefiting them by the way of nurturing life, though death they will not be double-minded;

units.zh: 以逸道勞之者，雖勤不怨。
units.en: make them work through measures that feel humane, and they will not resent even heavy duty.
units.literal: If by the way of ease you make them toil, though diligent they will not resent.

units.zh: 故其命可授，其力可竭，以戰則克，以攻則拔。
units.en: Then men will stake their lives and spend their last strength; fight and they win, strike and cities fall.
units.literal: Hence their lives may be entrusted, their strength may be exhausted; in battle they prevail, in attack they take cities.

units.zh: 是以善者慕德而安服，惡者畏懼而削跡。
units.en: The good embrace virtue and rest content; the wicked shrink back and vanish from sight.
units.literal: Hence the good admire virtue and submit in peace; the evil fear and erase their traces.

units.zh: 止戈而武，義實在文，唯任賢然後無患耳。
units.en: True martial virtue lays arms aside; its moral core lies in civil order—only when worthies hold office is the realm free of peril.
units.literal: To stop spears and thereby be martial—righteousness truly lies in patterning [culture]; only when worthies are employed is there then no trouble.

units.zh: 若夫水旱之災，自然理也。
units.en: Floods and droughts belong to nature's own pattern.
units.literal: As for flood and drought disasters, they are natural principle.

units.zh: 故古者三十年耕必有十年之儲，堯、湯遭之而人不困，有備故也。
units.en: Antiquity held ten years of grain for every thirty under the plough; Yao and Tang met drought and flood without famine because they were prepared.
units.literal: Hence in antiquity thirty years of farming necessarily had ten years of stores; Yao and Tang encountered them yet people were not distressed—because there was preparation.

units.zh: 自頃風雨雖頗不時，考之萬國，或境土相接，而豐約不同；
units.en: Lately the seasons have been somewhat awry, yet look across the commanderies: neighbors sharing a border may differ in feast or famine;
units.literal: Since lately wind and rain though somewhat untimely, examining the myriad states, some border lands adjoin yet abundance and want differ;

units.zh: 或頃畝相連，而成敗異流，固非天之必害於人，人實不能均其勞苦。
units.en: adjoining fields may thrive or fail side by side—Heaven does not single people out for harm; rulers and folk simply fail to spread hardship and ease evenly.
units.literal: or plots adjoin yet success and failure diverge—it is certainly not that Heaven necessarily harms people; people truly cannot equalize their toil and hardship.

units.zh: 失之於人，而求之於天，則有司惰職而不勸，百姓殆業而咎時，非所以定人志，致豐年也。
units.en: Blame Heaven while neglecting human causes and officials grow idle, commoners abandon their trades and curse the season—nothing there steadies the people's mind or fills the granaries.
units.literal: Missing it in men yet seeking it in Heaven—then officers slack in duty and do not exert themselves, common people neglect their work and blame the seasons—this is not the means to settle men's wills or bring abundant years.

units.zh: 宜勤人事而已。
units.en: Work diligently at what lies within human power—that is enough.
units.literal: One should diligently attend to human affairs—that is all.

units.zh: 臣誠愚鄙不足以奉對聖朝，猶進之於廷者，將使取諸其懷而獻之乎！
units.en: I am too dull to answer a sovereign court worthily—yet having been summoned into this hall, am I expected to lay bare whatever lies in my breast?
units.literal: Your servant is truly foolish and mean, not sufficient to respond to the sacred court—yet having advanced me to the hall, will you make me draw from my breast and present it!

units.zh: 臣懼不足也。
units.en: I fear I shall fall short.
units.literal: Your servant fears insufficiency.

units.zh: 若收不知言以致知言，臣則可矣，是以辭鄙不隱也。
units.en: If rough counsel may nonetheless yield insight, I may serve—so I hide none of my humble words.
units.literal: If by collecting ignorant speech one arrives at knowing speech, then your servant may suffice—hence my humble words are not concealed.

units.zh: 以對策上第，拜議郎。
units.en: He ranked first on the policy examination and was appointed Gentleman Consultant.
units.literal: By his examination answers ranking highest, he was appointed Gentleman Consultant.

units.zh: 母憂去職。
units.en: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.
units.literal: He left office for mourning his mother.

units.zh: 詵母病，苦無車，及亡，不欲車載柩，家貧無以市馬，乃於所住堂北壁外假葬，開戶，朝夕拜哭。
units.en: When Shen's mother fell ill, they suffered from having no cart; after she died he did not want the coffin carried by wagon—too poor to buy horses, he laid her in a temporary burial outside the north wall of the hall where he dwelt, opened a door, and bowed and wept morning and night.
units.literal: When Shen's mother fell ill, he suffered from having no cart; when she died, he did not wish to carry the coffin by cart—his household was poor and had no means to buy horses—so he buried her provisionally outside the north wall of the hall where he dwelt, opened a door, and morning and evening bowed and wept.

units.zh: 養雞種蒜，竭其方術。
units.en: He raised chickens and garlic by every scheme he could devise.
units.literal: He raised chickens and planted garlic, exhausting every expedient.

units.zh: 喪過三年，得馬八匹，輿柩至塚，負土成墳。
units.en: When three years of mourning had passed he owned eight horses; he bore the coffin to the grave on a litter and heaped earth into a mound.
units.literal: After three years of mourning he obtained eight horses, carried the coffin to the tomb on a litter, and piled earth to form the burial mound.

units.zh: 未畢，召為征東參軍。
units.en: Before the burial was complete he was summoned as army adjutant on the eastern campaign.
units.literal: Before it was finished, he was summoned as adjutant to the east-conquering expedition.

units.zh: 徙尚書郎，轉車騎從事中郎。
units.en: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat, then became adjutant to the General of Chariots and Cavalry.
units.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat, then promoted to adjutant with the household attendant for chariot and cavalry.

units.zh: 吏部尚書崔洪薦詵為左丞。
units.en: Cui Hong, Minister of Personnel, recommended Shen for the post of Assistant Director of the Left.
units.literal: Minister of Personnel Cui Hong recommended Shen for Assistant Director of the Left.

units.zh: 及在職，嘗以事劾洪，洪怨詵，詵以公正距之，語在《洪傳》。
units.en: Once in office he impeached Hong on a matter; Hong resented him, but Shen answered only with impartial rectitude—the story is told in Hong's biography.
units.literal: When in office, he once impeached Hong over an affair; Hong resented Shen, but Shen kept him at a distance with impartiality—the account is in Hong's biography.

units.zh: 洪聞而慚服。
units.en: When Hong learned of it he was mortified and yielded.
units.literal: Hong heard of it and felt ashamed and submitted.

units.zh: 累遷雍州刺史。
units.en: He advanced through several posts to Inspector of Yong Province.
units.literal: He was promoted by stages to Inspector of Yong Province.

units.zh: 武帝於東堂會送，問詵曰：「卿自以為何如？」
units.en: Emperor Wu hosted his farewell at the Eastern Hall and asked, "How do you rate yourself among men?"
units.literal: Emperor Wu saw him off at the Eastern Hall and asked Shen: "What do you consider yourself to be?"

units.zh: 詵對曰：「臣舉賢良對策，為天下第一，猶桂林之一枝，昆山之片玉。」
units.en: Xi Shen answered: "When I was examined as worthy and upright I placed first in the realm—no more than one twig on the cassia tree, one flake of jade from Mount Kun."
units.literal: Shen replied: "Your servant was recommended as worthy and upright and ranked first in the empire in the examination answers—like a single branch on the cassia tree, like a flake of jade from Kunlun."

units.zh: 帝笑。
units.en: The emperor laughed.
units.literal: The emperor laughed.

units.zh: 侍中奏免詵官，帝曰：「吾與之戲耳，不足怪也。」
units.en: The palace attendant memorialized to dismiss Shen; the emperor said, "We were only jesting—there is no offense."
units.literal: The attendant-in-chief memorialized to dismiss Shen from office; the emperor said: "I was merely joking with him—nothing to take amiss."

units.zh: 詵在任威嚴明斷，甚得四方聲譽。
units.en: In office he was austere, decisive, and clear-minded, and earned wide renown in every quarter.
units.literal: While in office Shen was stern, clear, and decisive, and won great reputation throughout the regions.

units.zh: 卒於官。
units.en: He died in post.
units.literal: He died in office.

units.zh: 子延登為州別駕。
units.en: His son Yan Deng became provincial aide-de-camp.
units.literal: His son Yan Deng served as provincial aide-de-camp.

units.zh: 阮種
units.en: Ruan Zhong.
units.literal: Ruan Zhong.

units.zh: 阮種，字德猷，陳留尉氏人，漢侍中胥卿八世孫也。
units.en: Ruan Zhong, courtesy name Deyou, came from Weishi in Chenliu—the eighth-generation descendant of Xu Qing, who served Han as palace attendant.
units.literal: Ruan Zhong, style Deyou, was a man of Weishi in Chenliu, eighth-generation descendant of Palace Attendant Xu Qing of Han.

units.zh: 弱冠有殊操，為嵇康所重。
units.en: Even as a young man he behaved unlike others; Xi Kang esteemed him.
units.literal: At the capping age he had unusual conduct and was esteemed by Xi Kang.

units.zh: 康著《養生論》，所稱阮生，即種也。
units.en: Xi Kang's "On Nourishing Life" praises "Master Ruan"—that man was Zhong.
units.literal: Kang wrote "On Nourishing Life"; the "Master Ruan" he praised was Zhong.

units.zh: 察孝廉，為公府掾。
units.en: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he served as a clerk in the metropolitan offices.
units.literal: He was nominated Filial and Incorrupt and served as clerk in the grand offices.

units.zh: 是時西虜內侵，災眚屢見，百姓饑饉，詔三公、卿尹、常伯、牧守各舉賢良方正直言之士。
units.en: Western tribes had crossed inward, omens kept appearing, and the people starved; an edict told the Three Dukes, senior ministers, imperial advisers, and governors each to nominate worthy men of integrity willing to speak plainly.
units.literal: At that time western barbarians invaded within the borders, calamities appeared repeatedly, the people starved; an edict ordered the Three Dukes, ministers and chief officers, constant attendants, and governors each to recommend worthy, good, and upright men prepared to speak plainly.

units.zh: 於是太保何曾舉種賢良。
units.en: Grand Guardian He Zeng thereupon nominated Zhong as worthy candidate.
units.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian He Zeng recommended Zhong as worthy and good.

units.zh: 策曰：「在昔哲王，承天之序，光宅宇宙，咸用規矩乾坤，惠康品類，休風流衍，彌於千載。
units.en: The examination topic ran: "Ancient sage kings received Heaven's mandate, illumined all within the cosmos, aligned Heaven and Earth by measure, brought peace to every kind of creature, and left transforming virtue echoing down a thousand years.
units.literal: The examination theme said: "Of old the wise kings, inheriting Heaven's sequence, brightly possessed the cosmos; all used regulation to align Heaven and Earth, kindly settled the myriad kinds; restorative influence flowed abroad and extended over a thousand ages.

units.zh: 朕應踐洪運統位，七載於今矣。
units.en: I have mounted the throne in answer to great fortune—seven years have now passed.
units.literal: We have answered to the great fortune of ruling the succession—seven years have passed to this day.

units.zh: 惟德弗嗣，不明於政，宵興惕厲，未燭厥猷。
units.en: Yet my virtue does not match my inheritance; I lack clarity in governing; I rise before dawn anxious and afraid—I have not yet discerned the right course.
units.literal: Yet virtue does not continue the legacy; We are unclear in government; We rise at midnight anxious and fearful—We have not illuminated that plan.

units.zh: 子大夫韞韥道術，儼然而進，朕甚嘉焉。
units.en: You bear the Way and its arts close within you and advance with dignity—I admire this deeply.
units.literal: You gentlemen have enfolded the Dao and its arts in your bosoms and advance with solemn bearing—We greatly admire this.

units.zh: 其各悉乃心，以闡喻朕志，深陳王道之本，勿有所隱，朕虛心以覽焉。」
units.en: Speak from the heart; unfold what I intend to ask; lay bare the foundations of the royal way; hide nothing—I listen with an open mind."
units.literal: Each exhaust your minds to clarify Our intent; deeply expound the root of the kingly way; conceal nothing—We will receive it with empty mind."

units.zh: 種對曰：「夫天地設位，聖人成能，王道至深，所以行化至遠。
units.en: Ruan Zhong replied: "Heaven and Earth fixed their stations and sages fulfilled their offices; the royal way runs deepest—therefore its transforming power reaches farthest.
units.literal: Zhong replied: "Heaven and Earth establish positions; sages complete their powers; the kingly way is utmost deep—hence transformation reaches far.

units.zh: 故能開物成務，而功業不匱，近無不聽，遠無不服，德逮群生，澤被區宇，聲施無窮，而典垂百代。
units.en: Thus they opened channels for human affairs and never exhausted true achievement; neighbors obeyed and distant peoples submitted; virtue touched every life, blessing soaked the realm, renown rolled on without end, and their pattern lasted for ages.
units.literal: Hence they can open things and accomplish tasks without exhausting merit; near, none fail to heed; far, none fail to submit; virtue reaches the multitude; grace spreads across the realm; fame extends without end; models hang for a hundred generations.

units.zh: 故《經》曰：'聖人久于其道，而天下化成。
units.en: The canon says, Hold fast long enough to the sage's path and the realm completes its transformation.
units.literal: Hence the Classic says: 'If the sage long persists in his way, all under Heaven is transformed and completed.

units.zh: '宜師蹤往代，襲跡三五，矯世更俗，以從人望。
units.en: Follow the footprints of earlier dynasties; walk in the wake of the sage rulers of highest antiquity; straighten the age and renew customs until they answer the people's hopes.
units.literal: One should take one's trail from former ages, tread in the footprints of the Three Five, correct the age and renew customs to follow men's hopes.

units.zh: 令率士遷義，下知所適，播醇美之化，杜邪枉之路，斯誠群黎之所欣想盛德而幸望休風也。」
units.en: Lead everyone under Heaven toward duty so common folk know their direction; spread untainted transformation and shut crooked byways—this is what the people long for when they dream of great virtue and pray for wholesome influence."
units.literal: Order all within the realm to move toward righteousness; below all will know where to go; broadcast pure and beautiful transformation; block crooked and wrong paths—this is truly what the multitude joyfully imagine in contemplating splendid virtue and fortunate hope for restorative influence.'"

units.zh: 又問政刑不宣，禮樂不立。
units.en: The examination further asked why government and punishments lacked clear expression and ritual and music stood unestablished.
units.literal: Again asked that government and punishments were not proclaimed, ritual and music not established.

units.zh: 對曰：「政刑之宣，故由乎禮樂之用。
units.en: He answered: "Clear government and punishments depend on putting ritual and music to use.
units.literal: He replied: "The proclamation of government and punishments indeed proceeds from the employment of ritual and music.

units.zh: 昔之明王，唯此之務，所以防遏暴慢，感動心術，制節生靈，而陶化萬姓也。
units.en: Enlightened kings of old made this their chief business—to curb violence and arrogance, stir heart and mind, give measure to the living, and shape the myriad clans.
units.literal: The enlightened kings of old made this their sole task—thereby to prevent and halt violence and arrogance, stir and move heart and technique, regulate and restrain the living, and mold and transform the myriad surnames.

units.zh: 禮以體德，樂以詠功，樂本於和，而禮師於敬矣。」
units.en: Ritual bodies forth virtue; music celebrates achievement; music springs from harmony; ritual models itself on reverence."
units.literal: Ritual embodies virtue; music sings merit; music roots in harmony; ritual takes reverence as its model.'"

units.zh: 又問戎蠻猾夏。
units.en: The examination further asked about frontier tribes troubling the heartland.
units.literal: Again asked about Rong and Man barbarians molesting the Xia.

units.zh: 對曰：「戎蠻猾夏，侵敗王略，雖古盛世，猶有此虞。
units.en: He answered: "When northern and southern tribes harass the Central Plains and wreck the royal strategy—even golden ages knew this fear.
units.literal: He replied: "When Rong and Man molest the Xia, invading and spoiling the royal plan—even in ancient flourishing ages there was still this anxiety.

units.zh: 故《詩》稱'獫狁孔熾'，《書》歎'蠻夷帥服'。
units.en: The Odes tells how the Xianyun blazed with violence; the Documents marvels when barbarian chiefs submit.
units.literal: Hence the Odes praises 'the Xianyun blaze fiercely'; the Documents sighs 'barbarians lead in submission.'

units.zh: 自魏氏以來，夷虜內附，鮮有桀悍侵漁之患。
units.en: Since the Wei settled surrendered tribes inside the frontier, we have rarely seen bold raiding or plunder.
units.literal: Since the Wei era, surrendered barbarians have dwelt within—there has seldom been the trouble of fierce arrogance and predatory aggression.

units.zh: 由是邊守遂怠，鄣塞不設。
units.en: That bred slackness along the border—forts and barriers went unmanned.
units.literal: On that account frontier defense grew slack and barrier passes were not manned.

units.zh: 而今醜虜內居，與百姓雜處，邊吏擾習，人又忘戰。
units.en: Now those tribes live mixed among the people; frontier officials grow used to turmoil and everyone forgets how to fight.
units.literal: Now the ugly barbarians dwell within, mingled with common people; frontier officers grow accustomed to disturbance and people forget war.

units.zh: 受方任者，又非其材，或以狙詐，侵侮邊夷；
units.en: The men charged with frontier posts often lack the right gifts—some bully border peoples with treachery;
units.literal: Those entrusted with regional duty are again not the right talent—some use cunning deceit and insult frontier barbarians;

units.zh: 或幹賞啗利，妄加討戮。
units.en: others chase bounties and profit and strike or kill without cause.
units.literal: some chase rewards and swallow profit and recklessly add executions.

units.zh: 夫以微羈而禦悍馬，又乃操以煩策，其不制者，固其理也。
units.en: Driving a restive mount on thin reins while flailing it with a cruel crop—you cannot expect control; the outcome follows of itself.
units.literal: To drive a fierce horse with thin reins and moreover wield a fussy whip—those who fail to control it, solidly it is the principle.

units.zh: 是以群醜蕩駭，緣間而動。
units.en: So every malcontent thrashes in panic and rises whenever a crack opens.
units.literal: Hence the mob of villains surges in alarm and stirs when opportunity appears.

units.zh: 雖三州覆敗，牧守不反，此非胡虜之甚勁，蓋用之者過也。
units.en: Three provinces collapsed and governors never returned—not because the Hu were invincible but because our own policies went wrong.
units.literal: Though three provinces were overturned and governors did not return—it is not that Hu barbarians were so strong; it is that those who used them went too far.

units.zh: 臣聞王者之伐，有征無戰，懷遠以德，不聞以兵。
units.en: I have heard that a true king's punishment means correction without endless war—he wins the far tribes by virtue, not by arms alone.
units.literal: I have heard that the king's punitive expeditions have punitive missions without battle; win the distant through virtue—I have not heard of doing so through arms.

units.zh: 夫兵凶器，而戰危事也。
units.en: Weapons are ill-starred tools; war is a deadly hazard.
units.literal: Arms are ill-omened tools; battle is a perilous affair.

units.zh: 兵興則傷農，眾集則費積；
units.en: Mobilize troops and the farms suffer; mass armies burn through the granaries;
units.literal: When arms arise, farming is harmed; when masses gather, stores are consumed.

units.zh: 農傷則人匱，積費則國虛。
units.en: hurt farming and the people go hungry; burn stores and the treasury empties.
units.literal: When farming is harmed, people are depleted; when stores are consumed, the state is emptied.

units.zh: 昔漢武之世，承文帝之業，資海內之富，役其材臣，以甘心匈奴，競戰勝之功，貪攻取之利，良將勁卒，屈於沙漠，勝敗相若，克不過當，夭百姓之命，填餓狼之口。
units.en: Under Han Wudi, building on Wendi's peace and the empire's wealth, he drove his able ministers to humble the Xiongnu—chasing glory in battle and profit in conquest—yet crack troops died in the sands; gains and losses balanced until triumph scarcely paid for itself while common lives fed desert wolves.
units.literal: In Emperor Wu's age of Han, inheriting Emperor Wen's enterprise, relying on the wealth within the seas, he employed his talented ministers to satisfy his heart toward the Xiongnu—competing for merit in victory in battle, greedy for gain in attack—good generals and crack troops collapsed in the desert; victory and defeat balanced; captures did not repay the cost—he cut short common people's lives to fill hungry wolves' maws.

units.zh: 及其以眾制寡，令匈奴遠跡，收功祁連，飲馬瀚海，天下之耗，已過太半矣。
units.en: When mass finally mastered scattered bands and drove the Xiongnu beyond reach—winning fame at Qilian and watering horses at the Han Sea—the realm had already spent more than half its strength.
units.literal: When later he used the many to control the few and made the Xiongnu flee far, he gathered merit at Qilian and watered horses at the Han Sea—but the empire's wastage had already passed half.

units.zh: 夫虛中國以事夷狄，誠非計之得者也。
units.en: Draining the heartland to chase steppe tribes is no sound strategy.
units.literal: To empty the Central Lands to serve barbarians is truly not a winning plan.

units.zh: 是以盜賊蜂起，山東不振。
units.en: Robbers swarmed and the eastern hills never recovered.
units.literal: Hence bandits rose like bees and east of the mountains did not revive.

units.zh: 暨宣元之時，趙充國征西零，馮奉世征南羌，皆兵不血刃，摧抑強暴，擒其首惡，此則折沖厭難，勝敗相辨，中世之明效也。」
units.en: Under Xuandi and Yuandi, Zhao Chongguo subdued the Xiling Qiang and Feng Fengshi the southern Qiang—both without drawing blood, crushing bullies and seizing ringleaders: real containment of disaster with costs and gains plain—the middle Han at its clearest."
units.literal: By the time of Emperors Xuan and Yuan, Zhao Chongguo campaigned against the Western Qiang and Feng Fengshi campaigned against the Southern Qiang—both without bloodying weapons, crushed the violent, seized their chiefs—this is turning back the shock and quelling disaster, victory and defeat clearly distinguished—the enlightened effect of middle antiquity.'"

units.zh: 又問咎征作見。
units.en: The examination further asked about ominous portents and their signs.
units.literal: Again asked about blame-signs appearing.

units.zh: 對曰：「陰陽否泰，六沴之災，則人主修政以禦之，思患而防之，建皇極之首，詳庶征之用。
units.en: He answered: "When yin and yang fall out of balance and the six calamities strike, the sovereign must mend policy to meet them, foresee danger and guard against it, set up the royal norm as guide, and weigh each portent as the Hongfan teaches.
units.literal: He replied: "When yin and yang are blocked or smooth, and disasters of the six excesses occur—the ruler cultivates government to withstand them, ponders peril and guards against them, establishes the supreme pole's guidance, and elaborates the employment of the many signs.

units.zh: 《詩》曰'敬之敬之，天惟顯思'，天聰明自我人聰明，是以人主祖承天命，日慎一日也。
units.en: The Odes warns, "Revere, revere—Heaven's light is watching"; Heaven hears through the people's hearing—so the Son of Heaven receives the mandate and grows more careful day by day.
units.literal: The Odes says 'Revere it, revere it—Heaven's brightness thinks'; Heaven's hearing and brightness come from our men's hearing and brightness—hence the ruler inherits Heaven's mandate and daily grows more cautious.

units.zh: 故能應受多福而永世克祚，此先王之所以退災消眚也。」
units.en: Thus he earns blessing and keeps the throne for generations—that is how earlier kings turned back calamity and cleared ill omens."
units.literal: Hence he can respond and receive abundant blessing and eternally preserve his throne—this is how former kings pushed back disaster and dispelled calamity.'"

units.zh: 又問經化之務。
units.en: The examination further asked about ordering society through moral teaching.
units.literal: Again asked about the tasks of classical transformation.

units.zh: 對曰：「夫王道之本，經國之務，必先之以禮義，而致人於廉恥。
units.en: He answered: "The royal way and the business of governing begin with ritual and right principle and lead people toward integrity and a sense of shame.
units.literal: He replied: "The root of the kingly way and the tasks of ordering the state must begin with ritual and righteousness and bring men to integrity and shame.

units.zh: 禮義立，則君子軌道而讓於善；
units.en: Establish ritual and principle and gentlemen keep to the Way and defer to the good;
units.literal: When ritual and righteousness stand, gentlemen track the way and yield to the good;

units.zh: 廉恥立，則小人謹行而不淫於制度。
units.en: instill integrity and shame and even common folk tread carefully and respect the law.
units.literal: when integrity and shame stand, petty men act cautiously and do not licentiously violate institutions.

units.zh: 賞以勸其能，威以懲其廢。
units.en: Rewards spur talent; authority punishes neglect.
units.literal: Reward encourages their ability; awe punishes their neglect.

units.zh: 此先王所以保乂定功，化洽黎元，而勳業長世也。
units.en: So the ancient kings preserved order, settled achievement, brought the people into harmony, and left a legacy for ages.
units.literal: This is how former kings preserved and settled merit, transformed and harmonized the black-haired people, and left merit lasting ages.

units.zh: 故上有克讓之風，則下有不爭之俗；
units.en: When the court breathes deference, the countryside loses its quarrels;
units.literal: Hence when above there is a wind of yielding overcoming, below there is a custom without contention;

units.zh: 朝有矜節之士，則野無貪冒之人。
units.en: when the capital keeps scrupulous ministers, the fields hold no grasping men.
units.literal: when at court there are scholars who restrain themselves, in the wilds there are no greedy people.

units.zh: 夫廉恥之於政，猶樹藝之有豐壤，良歲之有膏澤，其生物必油然茂矣。
units.en: Integrity and shame in government are rich soil for planting or spring rain in a good year—whatever sprouts there grows lush.
units.literal: Integrity and shame with respect to government are like fertile soil for planting trees or timely rain in a good year—what grows there must flourish lushly.

units.zh: 若廉恥不存，而惟刑是禦，則風俗凋弊，人失其性，錐刀之末，皆有爭心，雖峻刑嚴辟，猶不勝矣。
units.en: Without integrity and shame, rely on law alone and customs rot, nature warps, men quarrel over the slimmest gain—no severity of statute can contain them.
units.literal: If integrity and shame do not exist and only punishments are wielded, then customs wither and decay, men lose their nature; at the tip of an awl-blade all have contentious hearts—though punishments be harsh and executions severe, they still cannot overcome it.

units.zh: 其于政也，如農者之殖磽野，旱年之望豐穡，必不幾矣。
units.en: That is governance like sowing barren ground or expecting a bumper crop in drought—it cannot succeed.
units.literal: Applied to government it is like farmers planting barren soil or hoping for rich grain in a drought year—it assuredly will not succeed.

units.zh: 此三代所以享德長久，風醇俗美，皆數百年保天之祿。
units.en: This is why Xia, Shang, and Zhou kept virtue fresh and customs gentle for centuries—holding Heaven's mandate.
units.literal: This is why the Three Ages enjoyed virtue long-lasting, wind pure and customs fine—all preserved Heaven's blessing for centuries.

units.zh: 而秦二世而弊者，蓋其所由之塗殊也。」
units.en: Qin fell in two reigns because it walked another road altogether."
units.literal: Yet Qin collapsed in two generations—because the road they took was different.'"

units.zh: 又問：「將使武成七德，文濟九功，何路而臻於茲？
units.en: The examination asked further: "To fulfill the seven martial virtues and the nine civil accomplishments—what path reaches that goal?
units.literal: Again asked: "Desiring to realize the seven martial virtues and aid the nine civil accomplishments by culture—what road leads to this?

units.zh: 凡厥庶事，曷後曷先？」
units.en: Among every duty of state, what comes first and what after?"
units.literal: Of all these myriad tasks, what comes after and what before?"

units.zh: 對曰：「夫文武經德，所以成功丕業，咸熙庶績者，莫先於選建明哲，授方任能。
units.en: He answered: "To weave civil and military virtue into lasting achievement and bright government, nothing precedes choosing wise men, defining their posts, and empowering the capable.
units.literal: He replied: "As for civil and military threading virtue—whereby to accomplish great enterprise and harmoniously brighten the myriad tasks—nothing comes before selecting and establishing wise clarity, assigning regions and entrusting capability.

units.zh: 令才當其官而功稱其職，則萬機咸理，庶僚不曠。
units.en: Match talent to office and deeds to responsibility—then every branch of government runs and no seat stays empty.
units.literal: Order talent match office and merit match duty—then the myriad pivots are all ordered and no host of officials stands idle.

units.zh: 《書》曰：'天工人其代之。
units.en: The Documents says, Heaven's work—men stand in for it.
units.literal: The Documents says: 'Heaven's tasks man substitutes for them.

units.zh: '然則繼天理物，甯國安家，非賢無以成也。
units.en: Continue Heaven's pattern, order the realm, steady the house—without worthies nothing is finished.
units.literal: Thus continuing Heaven's pattern and ordering things, pacifying the state and settling the house—without worthies nothing is accomplished.

units.zh: 夫賢才之畜于國，由良工之須利器，巧匠之待繩墨也。
units.en: Stocking the state with talent is like a master carpenter needing sharp iron or a joiner waiting on his square.
units.literal: The storing of worthy talent in the state is like fine craftsmen needing sharp tools and clever artisans awaiting marking cords.

units.zh: 器用利，則斫削易而材不病；
units.en: Sharp tools make shaping easy and spare the timber;
units.literal: When tools are sharp, carving is easy and timber is not harmed;

units.zh: 繩墨設，則曲直正而眾形得矣。
units.en: true lines snap square and every joint fits.
units.literal: when marking cords are set, crooked and straight are corrected and all forms are obtained.

units.zh: 是以人主必勤求賢，而佚以任之也。
units.en: So the ruler must labor to find worthies, then may rule at ease once they serve.
units.literal: Hence the ruler must diligently seek worthies and then relax in employing them.

units.zh: 賢臣之於主，進則忠國愛人，退則砥節潔志，營職不幹私義，出心必由公途，明度量以呈其能，審經制以效其功。
units.en: A worthy minister serves his sovereign by advancing with loyalty to the realm and love for the people, withdrawing by burnishing integrity and clarifying purpose—duty never bows to private claims, counsel always follows the public road, measures display competence, and statutes prove results.
units.literal: Worthy ministers toward their lord—in advancing they are loyal to the state and cherish people; in retiring they polish integrity and cleanse aims; in managing duties they do not interfere with private righteousness; what issues from the heart must go by public paths; they clarify measures and degrees to display ability, examine norms and regulations to prove merit.

units.zh: 此昔之聖王所以恭己南面而化于陶鈞之上者，以其所任之賢與所賢之信也。
units.en: Ancient sage kings could sit facing south and shape the realm like clay on a wheel because they chose worthy men and trusted those they honored.
units.literal: This is why the sage kings of old could reverently fold themselves facing south and transform atop the potter's wheel—because those they employed were worthy and those they deemed worthy were trusted.

units.zh: 方今海內之士皆傾望休光，希心紫極，唯明主之所趣舍。
units.en: Scholars across the realm turn toward enlightened rule and fix their hopes on the throne—they watch only whom you advance or set aside.
units.literal: Now all scholars within the seas incline toward restorative radiance and fix their hearts on the purple pole—all awaits what the enlightened lord favors or rejects.

units.zh: 若開四聰之聽，廣疇咨之求，抽群英，延俊乂，考工授職，呈能制官，朝無素餐之士，如此化流罔極，樹功不朽矣。」
units.en: Open all four avenues of counsel, cast wide for advice, lift heroes from the ranks and welcome excellence—match craft to office and talent to title until no idler feeds at court—then transforming influence knows no bound and achievement never fades."
units.literal: If you open the hearing of the four counsels, broaden consultation from many fields, draw forth the throng of heroes, summon outstanding talents, examine workmanship and assign offices, display ability and regulate posts—so that at court none eat free meals—thus transformation will flow without limit and merit will stand imperishable.'"

units.zh: 時種與郤詵及東平王康俱居上第，即除尚書郎。
units.en: Zhong, Xi Shen, and Wang Kang of Dongping all placed at the top of the list and were immediately appointed Gentlemen of the Secretariat.
units.literal: At that time Zhong together with Xi Shen and Wang Kang of Dongping all ranked at the top—they were forthwith appointed Gentlemen of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 然毀譽之徒，或言對者因緣假託，帝乃更延群士，庭以問之。
units.en: Detractors claimed some answers rested on pull rather than merit, so the emperor convened another round of scholars for questioning in court.
units.literal: Yet among those who praise or slander, some said the respondents had relied on pretense by connections—thereupon the emperor extended audience to another throng of scholars and questioned them in the hall.

units.zh: 詔曰：「前者對策各指答所問，未盡子大夫所欲言，故復延見，其具陳所懷。
units.en: The edict ran: "Your first papers answered each question without saying all you hold back—so We summon you again; lay out everything on your mind.
units.literal: An edict said: "Earlier each answered the policy examination pointing to what was asked—not exhausting what you gentlemen wished to say—hence We extend audience again; fully set forth what you harbor in your breasts.

units.zh: 又比年連有水旱災眚，雖戰戰兢兢，未能究天人之理，當何修以應其變？
units.en: Year after year flood and drought pile up; though I tremble with care, I still cannot read Heaven's intentions—what must I cultivate to answer these omens?
units.literal: Moreover in successive years flood and drought calamities have linked together; though We tremble with fear, We have not yet fathomed the pattern of Heaven and man—what must be cultivated to respond to these changes?

units.zh: 人遇水旱饑饉者，何以救之？
units.en: When flood or drought brings famine—how should we rescue the people?
units.literal: When people encounter flood, drought, or famine—how shall they be saved?

units.zh: 中間多事，未得寧靜，思以省息煩務，令百姓不失其所。
units.en: Midway through endless crises we still lack calm—I wish to ease burdensome duties so the people keep their livelihoods.
units.literal: Amid many affairs in between We have not attained tranquillity; We wish by reducing and resting vexing tasks to order that common people do not lose their livelihood.

units.zh: 若人有所患苦者，有宜損益，使公私兩濟者，委曲陳之。
units.en: Where hardship could be eased by reform that helps both state and household—explain every turn of it.
units.literal: If people have sufferings that ought to be adjusted so both public and private benefit—set them forth in detail.

units.zh: 又政在得人，而知之至難，唯有因人視聽耳。
units.en: Government turns on having the right men, yet knowing minds is hardest—I must lean on what others see and hear.
units.literal: Moreover government lies in obtaining the right men—yet knowing them is extremely difficult—nothing but relying on others' seeing and hearing.

units.zh: 若有文武隱逸之士，各舉所知，雖幽賤負俗，勿有所限。
units.en: Whether civil or martial, in office or in hiding—each of you name whom you know; even the obscure, humble, or locally despised face no barrier.
units.literal: If there are scholars civil or martial, reclusive or hidden, each recommend those you know—even if obscure, lowly, or bearing ill repute from custom—place no limit.

units.zh: 故虛心思聞事實，勿務華辭，莫有所諱也。」
units.en: I empty my mind to hear truth—spurn ornament and withhold nothing."
units.literal: Hence We empty Our mind wishing to hear facts—do not strive at flowery rhetoric; hold nothing back.'"

units.zh: 種對曰：「伏惟陛下以聖哲玄覽，降䘏黎蒸，將濟元元，同之三代，旁求俊乂，以輔至化，此誠堯、舜之用心也。
units.en: Zhong answered: "Your Majesty in sage insight shelters the people, would lift the common folk to the level of the Three Ages, and casts wide for talent to perfect transformation—this is the heart of Yao and Shun.
units.literal: Zhong replied: "I humbly reflect that Your Majesty, with sagely wisdom and dark encompassing vision, lowers care upon the steaming multitude, about to rescue the common folk and align them with the Three Ages, broadly seeking outstanding talents to aid utmost transformation—this is truly the intent of Yao and Shun.

units.zh: 臣猥以頑魯之質，應清明之舉，前者對策，不足以疇塞聖詔，所陳不究，臣誠蒙昧，所以為罪。
units.en: I am coarse stuff answering a luminous summons; my first paper could not exhaust Your command—I spoke incompletely through sheer dullness; that is my fault.
units.literal: Your servant meanly with stubborn and dull substance answered the clear and bright summons—earlier the examination answers were insufficient to fill the sacred edict; what was set forth was not exhaustive—your servant is truly obtuse—thereby offense.

units.zh: 臣聞天生蒸庶，樹君以司牧之，人君道洽，則彝倫攸序，五福來備。
units.en: Heaven bred the multitude and set a ruler to shepherd them—when his course runs true, moral order settles and the five blessings gather.
units.literal: I have heard that Heaven produces the steaming multitude and sets up a lord to shepherd them; when the lord's way is harmonious, then constant norms are ordered and the five blessings arrive complete.

units.zh: 若政有愆失，刑理頗僻，則庶征不應，而淫亢為災。
units.en: When policy falters and justice skews, the portents refuse to align—drought or flood follows as scourge.
units.literal: If government errs and punishments and principle are quite biased, then the many signs do not respond and excessive drought or flood becomes disaster.

units.zh: 此則天人之理，而興廢之由也。
units.en: Such is the bond between Heaven and humanity—the hinge of rise and ruin.
units.literal: This then is the pattern of Heaven and man—and the cause of rise and fall.

units.zh: 昔之聖王，政道備而制先具，軌人以務，致之於本，是以雖有水旱之眚，而無饑饉之患也。
units.en: Ancient kings finished policy before crisis came—tasks guided men back to fundamentals—so drought or flood never slid into famine.
units.literal: The sage kings of old had the way of government complete and institutions prepared beforehand; they tracked men by tasks and brought them to the root—hence though there were flood and drought calamities, there was no famine distress.

units.zh: 自頃陰陽隔並，水旱為災，亦猶期運之致。
units.en: Lately yin and yang clash—flood and drought follow—the times themselves bring such rounds.
units.literal: Since lately yin and yang have blocked and doubled—water and drought became disasters—it is still what appointment of fortune brings.

units.zh: 不然，則亦有司之不帥，不能宣承聖德，以讚揚大化，故和氣未降而人事未敘也。
units.en: Or else officials fail to lead—unable to voice Your virtue and lift great transformation—so benign qi withholds itself and human affairs stay tangled.
units.literal: If not so—then there are also officers who do not lead, unable to proclaim and inherit sagely virtue to assist and spread great transformation—hence harmonizing qi has not descended and human affairs are not ordered.

units.zh: 方今百姓凋弊，公私無儲，誠在於休役靜人，勸嗇務分，此其救也。
units.en: People are exhausted and neither granaries nor households hold surplus—the cure is lighter levies, calmer lives, thrift, and fair shares.
units.literal: Now common people are withered and exhausted; public and private lack stores—the truth lies in resting corvée and quieting people, urging thrift and dividing labor—this is the remedy.

units.zh: 人之所患，由於役煩網密而通道未孚也。
units.en: Their grief springs from endless labor, tangled law, and rulers who never earn trust.
units.literal: What people suffer comes from vexing corvée and tight nets while the open way is not trusted.

units.zh: 役煩則百姓失業，網密則下背其誠，通道未孚則人無固志。
units.en: Heavy corvée steals livelihoods; harsh surveillance breeds deceit; absent trust leaves no loyal heart.
units.literal: When corvée is vexing, common people lose their livelihood; when nets are tight, those below betray their sincerity; when the open way is not trusted, men lack steadfast will.

units.zh: 此則損益之至務，安危之大端也。
units.en: Here is the chief lever of reform—the hinge of survival itself.
units.literal: This then is the utmost task of reduction and augmentation—the great hinge of safety and danger.

units.zh: 傳曰：'始與善，善進，則不善蔑由至。
units.en: Tradition says, Start with good—when goodness advances, evil finds no door.
units.literal: The tradition says: 'Begin with the good; when good advances, then evil has no path to arrive.

units.zh: '孔子曰：'視其所以，觀其所由，人焉廋哉！
units.en: Confucius said, Watch what he does and how he does it—how then can a man hide?
units.literal: Confucius said: 'Look at what he does; observe his means—how can men hide!

units.zh: '若夫文武隱逸之士，幽賤負俗之才，故非愚臣之所能識。
units.en: As for hidden civil and martial talents, obscure men scorned by local gossip—they lie beyond my dull wit.
units.literal: As for civil and martial reclusive scholars and obscure lowly talents bearing ill repute—they are truly not what your foolish servant can recognize.

units.zh: 謹竭愚以對。」
units.en: I answer to the limit of my ignorance."
units.literal: I respectfully exhaust stupidity in answering.'"

units.zh: 策奏，帝親覽焉，又擢為第一。
units.en: When his paper reached the throne, the emperor read it himself and again ranked him first.
units.literal: When the examination memorial was submitted, the emperor personally reviewed it and again promoted him to first place.

units.zh: 轉中書郎。
units.en: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
units.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 進止有方，正已率下，朝廷咸憚其威容。
units.en: Measured in advance and retreat, he set the standard below him—the court stood in awe of his bearing.
units.literal: In advancing and halting he had method; correcting himself he led those below—the court all feared his imposing bearing.

units.zh: 每為駁議，事皆施用，遂為楷則。
units.en: His dissenting memorials were always adopted and became precedents.
units.literal: Whenever he composed counter-memorials, the affairs were all adopted—thereupon they became models.

units.zh: 遷平原相。
units.en: He was promoted to chancellor of Pingyuan.
units.literal: He was promoted to Chancellor of Pingyuan.

units.zh: 時襄邑衛京自南陽太守遷于河內，與種俱拜，帝望而歎曰：「二千石皆若此，朕何憂乎！」
units.en: Wei Jing of Xiangyi transferred from Prefect of Nanyang to Henei and was invested together with Zhong; the emperor watched them and sighed, "If every two-thousand-bushel official looked like this, what should I fear?"
units.literal: At that time Wei Jing of Xiangyi transferred from Prefect of Nanyang to Henei—he was invested together with Zhong; the emperor looked on them and sighed: "If all two-thousand-bushel officials were like this, what would We have to worry about!"

units.zh: 種為政簡惠，百姓稱之，卒於郡。
units.en: Zhong ruled with restraint and kindness; the people praised him and he died in office.
units.literal: Zhong's government was simple and kind; common people praised him—he died in the commandery.

units.zh: 華譚
units.en: Hua Tan.
units.literal: Hua Tan.

units.zh: 華譚，字令思，廣陵人也。
units.en: Hua Tan, courtesy name Ling Si, came from Guangling.
units.literal: Hua Tan, style Ling Si, was a man of Guangling.

units.zh: 祖融，吳左將軍、錄尚書事。
units.en: His grandfather Rong had been General of the Left in Wu and Recorder of Secretariat affairs.
units.literal: His grandfather Rong was General of the Left of Wu and Recorder of Secretariat affairs.

units.zh: 父諝，吳黃門郎。
units.en: His father Xu served Wu as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
units.literal: His father Xu was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate of Wu.

units.zh: 譚期歲而孤，母年十八，便守節鞠養，動勞備至。
units.en: Tan lost his father at one year; his eighteen-year-old mother kept her widowhood and raised him through every hardship.
units.literal: Tan was orphaned at one full year; his mother was eighteen years old—she then maintained her widow integrity and raised him, labor and toil reaching the utmost.

units.zh: 及長，好學不倦，爽慧有口辯，為鄰里所重。
units.en: Grown to manhood he studied tirelessly—bright, articulate, respected by neighbors.
units.literal: When grown, he loved learning without tiring; he was bright and clever with skill in debate—esteemed by neighbors and village.

units.zh: 揚州刺史周浚引為從事史，愛其才器，待以賓友之禮。
units.en: Zhou Jun, Inspector of Yang Province, took him on as clerk—valuing his talent, he treated him as guest and friend.
units.literal: Inspector of Yang Province Zhou Jun appointed him clerk of staff—he loved his talent and capacity and treated him with guest-friend ritual.

units.zh: 太康中，刺史嵇紹舉譚秀才，將行，別駕陳總餞之，因問曰：「思賢之主以求才為務，進取之士以功名為先，何仲舒不仕武帝之朝，賈誼失分漢文之時？
units.en: During Taikang, Ji Shao nominated Tan as cultivated talent; as Tan prepared to leave, Chen Zong, his aide, hosted a farewell and asked: "Sage rulers hunger for talent; ambitious men chase fame—why did Dong Zhongshu refuse Emperor Wu, and Jia Yi miss his moment under Emperor Wen?
units.literal: In the Taikang era, Inspector Ji Shao nominated Tan as cultivated talent; about to depart, aide-de-camp Chen Zong gave him a farewell feast and thereupon asked: "Worthy lords take seeking talent as their task; advancing scholars take merit and fame first—why did Dong Zhongshu not serve Emperor Wu's court, and Jia Yi miss his fit under Emperor Wen of Han?

units.zh: 此吳、晉之滯論，可辨此理而後別。」
units.en: Wu and Jin brood over this stale puzzle—answer it clearly and we may part."
units.literal: This is a stale debate of Wu and Jin—one may clarify this principle and then take leave."

units.zh: 譚曰：「夫聖人在上，物無不理，百揆之職，非賢不居。
units.en: Tan replied: "When sages sit on high, nothing stays unordered—no post falls to anyone but the worthy.
units.literal: Tan said: "When sages are above, nothing is not ordered; posts of the hundred affairs—none but the worthy occupy them.

units.zh: 故山林無匿景，衡門不棲遲。
units.en: So hills hide no recluse worth hiring and cottage gates shelter no loiterer.
units.literal: Hence in mountains and forests no brightness hides; at a hemp gate none linger idle.

units.zh: 至承統之王，或是中才，或復凡人，居聖人之器，處兆庶之上，是以其教日穨，風俗漸弊。
units.en: Heirs who inherit power may be middling or merely ordinary yet wield the sage's authority over millions—teaching frays and customs rot.
units.literal: When it comes to heirs who inherit the line—some are middling talent, some again common men—dwelling in the sage's vessel, placed above the myriad million—thereby their instruction daily declines and customs gradually spoil.

units.zh: 又中才之君，所資者偏，物以類感，必於其黨，黨言雖非，彼以為是。
units.en: Mediocre rulers lean on partial counselors—like calls to like inside their clique—wrong counsel sounds right to them.
units.literal: Moreover middling-talent lords rely on biased advisers—things move by kindred sympathy and surely toward their faction—faction speech though wrong, they take as right.

units.zh: 以所授有顏、冉之賢，所用有廊廟之器，居官者日冀元凱之功，在上者日庶堯、舜之義，彼豈知其政漸毀哉！
units.en: Give them ministers like Yan Hui and Ran Geng and tools fit for the ancestral hall—officials dream of Eight Yuan merit and rulers dream of Yao and Shun—yet they never see policy rotting beneath them!
units.literal: Suppose those appointed had the worth of Yan and Ran and those employed had hall-and-temple vessels—officeholders daily hoped for Yuan and Kai's merit; those above daily hoped for Yao and Shun's righteousness—how could they know their government gradually ruined!

units.zh: 朝雖有求賢之名，而無知才之實。
units.en: Court keeps the slogan of seeking talent without the substance of judging it.
units.literal: Though court had the name of seeking worthies, there was no reality of recognizing talent.

units.zh: 言雖當，彼以為誣；
units.en: Truth they call slander;
units.literal: Speech though right, they took as slander;

units.zh: 策雖奇，彼以為妄。
units.en: sound policy they dismiss as fantasy.
units.literal: policy though marvelous, they took as wild.

units.zh: 誣則毀己之言入，妄則不忠之責生，豈故為哉？
units.en: Label counsel slander and self-serving flattery floods in; call it mad and charges of disloyalty follow—not by accident.
units.literal: When it is slander, words that ruin oneself enter; when wild, charge of disloyalty arises—is it purposely so?

units.zh: 淺明不見深理，近才不睹遠體也。
units.en: Shallow judgment cannot grasp depth; petty talent cannot see the whole.
units.literal: Shallow clarity does not see deep principle; near talent does not behold distant scope.

units.zh: 是以言不用，計不施，恐死亡之不暇，何論功名之立哉！
units.en: Plans shelved and counsel ignored—men barely survive—what hope of fame?
units.literal: Hence counsel is not used, plans not deployed—fearing they have no leisure for death—what talk of establishing merit and fame!

units.zh: 故上官昵而屈原放，宰嚭寵而伍員戮，豈不哀哉！
units.en: Shangguan Jin won favor and Qu Yuan went into exile; Bo Pi rose and Wu Zixu died—what sorrow!
units.literal: Hence Shangguan was intimate and Qu Yuan was banished; Zai Pi was favored and Wu Yuan was executed—is it not lamentable!

units.zh: 若仲舒抑于孝武，賈誼失于漢文，蓋復是其輕者耳。
units.en: Dong Zhongshu slighted under Emperor Wu and Jia Yi stalled under Emperor Wen—among failures those rank as mild.
units.literal: As for Dong Zhongshu suppressed under Xiaowu, Jia Yi missing fit under Han Wen—those are still the lighter cases.

units.zh: 故白起有云：『非得賢之難，用之難。
units.en: Bai Qi said, "Finding talent is easy—using it is hard.
units.literal: Hence Bai Qi had a saying: 'It is not hard to obtain worthies—it is hard to employ them.

units.zh: 非用之難，信之難。』
units.en: Using talent is easy—trusting it is hard."
units.literal: It is not hard to employ them—it is hard to trust them.

units.zh: 得賢而不能用，用而不能信，功業豈可得而成哉！」
units.en: Talent unused or trusted too late never builds an empire."
units.literal: Obtain worthies yet cannot employ them; employ yet cannot trust them—how can merit and enterprise be accomplished!'"

units.zh: 譚至洛陽，武帝親策之曰：「今四海一統，萬里同風，天下有道，莫斯之盛。
units.en: When Tan reached Luoyang, Emperor Wu examined him in person: "The realm is one; customs align for ten thousand li—never has the Way shone brighter.
units.literal: When Tan arrived at Luoyang, Emperor Wu personally examined him, saying: "Now the four seas are unified, ten thousand li share one wind; all under Heaven has the Way—none surpasses this flourishing.

units.zh: 然北有未羈之虜，西有醜施之氐，故謀夫未得高枕，邊人未獲晏然，將何以長弭斯患，混清六合？」
units.en: Yet northern tribes remain outside the halter and western Di bands still stir—counselors cannot sleep easy nor border folk rest—how may we end these troubles and clear the whole realm?"
units.literal: Yet north there are unsubdued captives; west there are Choushi Di—hence strategists cannot pillow high and frontier folk do not obtain tranquillity—how shall We long quell these troubles and clarify and purify the six directions?"

units.zh: 對曰：「臣聞聖人之臨天下也，祖乾綱以流化，順穀風以興仁，兼三才以禦物，開四聰以招賢。
units.en: He answered: "Sages who rule the realm anchor transformation in Heaven's pattern, ride the east wind of spring to nurture kindness, wield heaven-earth-man together, and open every avenue of counsel to draw worthies.
units.literal: He replied: "I have heard that when sages face all under Heaven, they take Heaven's guiding net as ancestor to spread transformation, comply with grain wind to raise benevolence, combine the three powers to manage things, open the four counsels to summon worthies.

units.zh: 故勞謙日昃，務在擇才，宣明岩穴，垂光隱滯。
units.en: They toil humbly past noon—talent is everything—shine light into caves and lift men stalled in shadow.
units.literal: Hence laboring in humility till sunset, the task lies in choosing talent, proclaiming brightness from cliff caves, shedding light on hidden obstruction.

units.zh: 俊乂龍躍，帝道以光；
units.en: Heroes rise like dragons—the royal path gleams;
units.literal: Outstanding talents leap like dragons—the emperor's way thereby shines;

units.zh: 清德風翔，王化克舉。
units.en: pure virtue rides the wind—kingly transformation takes hold.
units.literal: pure virtue wind-soars—kingly transformation is able to rise.

units.zh: 是以皋陶見舉，不仁者遠；
units.en: Gaoyao once lifted—the cruel fled;
units.literal: Hence when Gaoyao was promoted, the unkindly stood far off;

units.zh: 陸賈重漢，遠夷折節。
units.en: Lu Jia lent Han weight—distant tribes bowed.
units.literal: Lu Jia esteemed Han—distant barbarians bent the knee.

units.zh: 今聖朝德音發於帷幄，清風翔乎無外，戎旗南指，江、漢席捲；
